cd <repo>
ethos mission dispatch \
  --worker bwk \
  --evaluator rsc \
  --type design \
  --write-set "docs/design-opencode-plugin.md,DESIGN.md" \
  --criteria "Fix a structural harness-parity defect the operator identified by reading internal/enable/enable.go directly: that file's deposit logic (CanonicalImport = '@.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md', claudemd.Register) is itself Claude-Code-specific, not harness-neutral. The design's current Sec5 point 4 and Sec1.1 propose 'ethos enable --opencode' as a flag bolted onto this existing Claude-Code-flavored 'ethos enable' command. That shape is wrong: it makes Claude Code the unqualified default and OpenCode an opt-in qualifier, which contradicts the spec's own HarnessNeutrality theorem in spirit even though the Registry data model itself stays neutral. Restructure the design (and DESIGN.md's DES-078 mirror) so neither harness is privileged: propose something like 'ethos enable claude' / 'ethos enable opencode' as coequal subcommands (or an equivalent flagging scheme with NO privileged bare form that silently means Claude Code), each depositing that harness's own native artifact -- the existing CLAUDE.md import for Claude Code, the opencode.json plugin registration for OpenCode -- with neither implied by the other. A repo using both harnesses runs both commands explicitly; running one must not silently also enable or skip the other." \
  --criteria "Add a new subsection (or expand Sec2 appropriately) stating a confirmed fact the operator surfaced and the leader verified directly against docs/spec-opencode-integration.tex Sec'Harness Instantiation': the design's fork-propagation machinery (Sec2.2, Sec2.3, Sec2.3.2's claim-forked primitive) is NOT OpenCode-specific and must not be framed as if it were. The spec's own Harness Instantiation section, Case 2 ('--fork-session/`/fork`/`/branch`'), found on direct verification that Claude Code's own --fork-session, /fork, and /branch commands mint a genuine new top-level session exactly like OpenCode's session.fork, and a SessionStart hook already reports source: 'fork' to distinguish it (cited: Claude Code v2.1.214, code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md). The spec states Claude Code's ForkNeverInheritsClaim guarantee is NOT vacuous for this case and needs the SAME session-level claim-isolation treatment OpenCode gets -- but nothing in the current Go codebase (internal/mission/, internal/hook/) implements this for Claude Code today; the leader grepped and confirmed no AllocateDelegationForkPropagated-shaped primitive exists anywhere. State plainly in the design: claim-forked and the Roster.ParentSession field (Sec2.3.2) are harness-neutral Go primitives with NO OpenCode-specific logic in them; wiring Claude Code's own SessionStart hook to call session create --parent-session and claim-forked when it observes source: 'fork' is additional, closely related implementation work this design's Sec5 should name as in-scope for the SAME implementation stage (not a separate future concern), since building claim-forked only for OpenCode and leaving Claude Code's identical gap open would itself reintroduce a parity difference between harnesses." \
  --criteria "Review the rest of the document (all sections) for any other place where OpenCode is framed as an add-on, extension, or afterthought to a Claude-Code baseline rather than a coequal harness instantiation of the same Registry model, and correct the framing. Do not rewrite content that is already harness-neutral; this is a wording/framing audit, not new technical content, except for the two substantive items above." \
  --criteria "Do NOT touch, read, or stage .punt-labs/vox/vox.md -- it has an unrelated uncommitted modification from the vox daemon that must be left alone. If your git add picks it up accidentally, unstage it before committing." \
  --criteria "Run make check before each commit and record it in the mission result evidence." \
  --criteria "Commit incrementally -- one commit per logical fix. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes." \
  --context "Round 4 of the design-stage mission for ethos-5y4r's DES-078, PR #536 (https://github.com/punt-labs/ethos/pull/536), branch design/opencode-plugin-adapter -- already checked out, DO NOT create a new branch or touch main. The operator (not an automated reviewer this time) personally identified this round's core finding by reading internal/enable/enable.go and pushing back on the leader's own incorrect assumption that the existing 'ethos enable' deposit path was harness-neutral. This is an explicit product/design principle from the operator: OpenCode is a first-class, coequal harness, not a secondary option layered onto Claude Code. Push commits to origin design/opencode-plugin-adapter (already tracked) to update the existing PR -- do not open a new PR." \
  --ticket ethos-5y4r \
  --budget 2 2>&1

tool_input.prompt:
You are bwk, working ethos mission m-2026-10-21-003. Run `ethos mission show m-2026-10-21-003` first to read your full contract (write-set, success criteria, context) — follow it exactly.

CRITICAL: confirm with `git branch --show-current` that you are on `design/opencode-plugin-adapter` (the head of open PR #536, https://github.com/punt-labs/ethos/pull/536) before your first commit. Do NOT create a new branch. Do NOT touch `main`. Push with `git push origin design/opencode-plugin-adapter`.

CRITICAL: there is an unrelated uncommitted change to `.punt-labs/vox/vox.md` in this working tree (a vox daemon-managed config file). Do not read, touch, or stage it. If a broad `git add` picks it up, unstage it (`git restore --staged .punt-labs/vox/vox.md`) before committing — never commit that file as part of this mission.

Background: this is round 4 of revisions to docs/design-opencode-plugin.md and DESIGN.md's DES-078 entry, for bead ethos-5y4r. Rounds 1-3 fixed defects found by automated PR reviewers (Qodo, Copilot, Cursor Bugbot) and by the leader's own direct research (context7, a real GitHub PR, direct repo reads). This round's finding came from the human operator directly — they read `internal/enable/enable.go` themselves and caught something the leader had gotten wrong.

**The core finding:** `internal/enable/enable.go`'s existing deposit logic (`CanonicalImport = "@.punt-labs/ethos/CLAUDE.md"`, `claudemd.Register`) is Claude-Code-specific, not harness-neutral — it writes a `CLAUDE.md` import, which only Claude Code reads. The design doc's current Sec5 point 4 and Sec1.1 propose `ethos enable --opencode` as a flag bolted onto this existing Claude-Code-flavored `ethos enable` command. That's the wrong shape: it makes Claude Code the unqualified default and OpenCode an opt-in qualifier. The operator was explicit about the principle: **OpenCode is a first-class, coequal harness — not a secondary option layered onto Claude Code.** This must be visible in the design's own command surface, not just in the Registry's internal data model (which the spec's `HarnessNeutrality` theorem already covers).

Your job, per the contract's 3 substantive criteria:

1. Restructure the enablement command proposal so neither harness is privileged — e.g. `ethos enable claude` / `ethos enable opencode` as coequal subcommands, or an equivalent scheme with no privileged bare form. Each deposits its own harness's native artifact (CLAUDE.md import for Claude Code; opencode.json plugin registration for OpenCode). Running one must not silently enable or skip the other. Mirror this into DESIGN.md's DES-078 entry.

2. Add a new subsection (or expand Sec2) stating a confirmed fact: the design's fork-propagation machinery (Sec2.2, Sec2.3, Sec2.3.2's `claim-forked` primitive) is NOT OpenCode-specific. The formal spec's own "Harness Instantiation" section, discussing Claude Code's `--fork-session`/`/fork`/`/branch` commands, found on direct verification that these mint a genuine new top-level Claude Code session exactly like OpenCode's `session.fork`, and that a `SessionStart` hook already reports `source: "fork"` to distinguish it (cited in the spec: Claude Code v2.1.214, code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md). The spec states Claude Code's `ForkNeverInheritsClaim` guarantee is NOT vacuous for this case and needs the SAME session-level claim-isolation treatment OpenCode gets — but nothing in the current Go codebase implements this for Claude Code today (the leader confirmed by grep: no `AllocateDelegationForkPropagated`-shaped primitive exists anywhere in `internal/mission/` or `internal/hook/`). State plainly: `claim-forked` and the `Roster.ParentSession` field are harness-neutral Go primitives with no OpenCode-specific logic in them. Name wiring Claude Code's own `SessionStart` hook to call `session create --parent-session` and `claim-forked` when it observes `source: "fork"` as additional, closely related work that belongs in the SAME implementation stage's scope (Sec5) — not a separate future concern — because building `claim-forked` only for OpenCode while leaving Claude Code's identical gap open would itself reintroduce the parity difference the operator is trying to avoid.

3. Read through the whole document and correct any other place where OpenCode reads as an add-on/extension/afterthought to a Claude-Code baseline rather than a coequal harness instantiation. This is a wording/framing audit on top of items 1-2, not new technical content elsewhere — do not rewrite sections that are already harness-neutral in substance.

Run `make check` (not just `make docs`) before each commit, and record it in your mission result evidence.

When done, submit your result via `ethos mission result` per the contract, push your commits to `origin design/opencode-plugin-adapter`, then stop — do not advance or close the mission, and do not touch the PR itself. The leader reviews and closes.
